prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided web search results, here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports as a burden.

The curl project, led by Daniel Stenberg, has been the most vocal about the specific burden of "AI slop" in its security vulnerability reporting process. The provided sources detail a progression from initial concern to implementing a checkbox for AI disclosure, and finally to the drastic step of terminating its bug bounty program altogether due to the unsustainable burden.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "I have previously blogged about the relatively new trend of AI slop in vulnerability reports submitted to curl and how it hurts and exhausts us." | CLAIM: The curl security team finds AI-generated vulnerability reports exhausting and harmful.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Every report thus engages 3-4 persons. Perhaps for 30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each." | CLAIM: Each low-quality report consumes a significant amount of time from multiple maintainers.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: Dealing with these reports has a negative emotional impact on the maintainers.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: The volume of invalid AI reports is compared to a Denial-of-Service attack.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "He went on to say that the project has never received a single valid bug report that was generated using AI, and their rate is increasing." | CLAIM: All AI-generated reports submitted to curl have been invalid, and the number is growing.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "“A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time,” wrote Daniel Stenberg" | CLAIM: The burden of AI slop has reached a critical, unsustainable level for the curl team.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly... they just hand it over to us and we get a couple of hours of work per every such instance." | CLAIM: Maintainers view low-effort AI submissions as a form of abuse that transfers hours of work to them.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "Previously, I mean two years ago, every such report, it actually meant that the reporter... actually invested something... That balance is off now." | CLAIM: AI has broken the previous balance where reporters had to invest their own time to validate a bug.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bug-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "The project developer for one of the Internet’s most popular networking tools is scrapping its vulnerability reward program after being overrun by a spike in the submission of low-quality reports, much of it AI-generated slop." | CLAIM: The burden of AI slop directly led to the termination of curl's bug bounty program.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bug-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "“We need to make moves to ensure our survival and intact mental health.”" | CLAIM: The primary reason for ending the program was to protect the well-being of the maintainers.

The provided sources also confirm that Seth Larson, a security developer for the Python Software Foundation, has raised similar concerns, indicating this is not a problem isolated to a single project.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Python's Seth Larson also raised concerns about these AI slop reports back in December, saying that responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: A Python maintainer confirmed that AI reports are costly to investigate because they appear legitimate.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "“Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports,” Larson wrote. “All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: AI slop reports contribute to maintainer burnout through stress and isolation.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Specific, direct quotes from Seth Larson's original December blog post (the provided source only quotes a secondary article quoting him).
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Public reports from maintainers of other large open-source projects (e.g., Linux kernel, Kubernetes, Apache Foundation projects) about the burden of AI-generated PRs or bug reports. The provided sources only cover curl and Python.
